judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag or challenge the description of the parametric model attributed to Middleton et al. 2016, nor does the reviewer mention the missing 'Schechter-like' qualifier or challenge the methodological description against the cited source.

The review does not mention Middleton et al. 2016, the Schechter-like model description, or any citation support problem in Sec. IV. There is no challenge to the post-edit claim against its cited source.
The reviewer does not mention the Middleton et al. 2016 paper or the description of the merger-density model in Section IV, and therefore fails to flag the removal of the 'Schechter-like' qualifier.
The reviewer does not flag any inconsistency between the Discussion section's 24% figure and the Results section's 23% figure for the IPTA DR3 detection probability under the M2 model.

The reviewer discusses SNR values and Figure 5 but does not flag an internal inconsistency between the Discussion's 24% claim and the Results section's 23% claim for IPTA DR3 under model M2. No specific numerical mismatch is identified.

The reviewer does not mention or challenge the appended asymptotic limit claim 'lim_{tau_a -> tau_c} f_orb^(P,a) = 0' appended to the pulsar-term orbital frequency equation; no mathematical errors in that equation are flagged.

The review comments on Equation 12 and notation near Equations 1 and 10, but never mentions Eq. (forbP-a), the appended limit statement, or the asymptotic value of the pulsar-term orbital frequency as tau_a approaches tau_c.
The reviewer provides comments on Equations 1, 10, and 12, but does not mention Equation (forbP-a) or the mathematically incorrect limit claim appended to it.

The reviewer does not flag the homophone swap of 'effect' to 'affect' in the Methods sentence about binary mass ratio's influence on detection efficiency; no typographical or grammatical error of this kind is mentioned.

Although the reviewer includes minor typographical comments, they do not identify the specific homophone error 'negligible affect' versus 'negligible effect' in Sec. 3. No corresponding typo flag appears.
The reviewer discusses the scientific assumption of the binary mass ratio in Section III but does not notice or flag the 'affect' for 'effect' homophone typo in that section.
